# Results and Findings

*All numerical values in this document are sourced directly from the CSV outputs generated by the `Unified_Analysis/` pipeline scripts. Each section cites its source file(s) so every claim is traceable.*

## 1. Dataset Overview

**Source:** [`data_quality_audit.csv`](Unified_Analysis/data_quality_audit.csv), [`comparability_matrix.csv`](Unified_Analysis/comparability_matrix.csv), [`replicate_structure.csv`](Unified_Analysis/replicate_structure.csv)

### 1.1 Master Dataset Composition

The harmonized master dataset contains **302 observations** across seven sub-phases:

| Sub-phase | Phase Group | n | CR range (mm/yr) | CR mean (mm/yr) | CR std (mm/yr) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1-DoE-Blend | P1 | 28 | 1.637 – 12.900 | 3.739 | 3.733 |
| P1-Temperature | P1 | 30 | 10.108 – 231.710 | 97.408 | 82.552 |
| P1-Time | P1 | 30 | 2.359 – 19.837 | 5.600 | 5.422 |
| P2-Temperature | P2 | 90 | 2.100 – 513.400 | 111.724 | 123.180 |
| P2-Time | P2 | 90 | 2.000 – 99.900 | 15.524 | 15.166 |
| P3-Okro-Acid | P3 | 17 | 35.068 – 124.736 | 84.111 | 26.185 |
| P3-Okro-Basic | P3 | 17 | -42.073 – 885.788 | 71.535 | 213.430 |
| **Total** | | **302** | | | |

*Source: `data_quality_audit.csv`, columns `Study`, `n`, `CR_min`, `CR_max`, `CR_mean`, `CR_std`.*

### 1.2 Data Quality Flags

| Sub-phase | Missing Temp_C | Missing Time_h | Missing IE% | Duplicate rows | CR ≤ 0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1-DoE-Blend | 28 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| P1-Temperature | 0 | 30 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| P1-Time | 30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| P2-Temperature | 0 | 0 | 15 | 0 | 0 |

| P3-Okro-Acid | 0 | 17 | 17 | 0 | 0 |
| P3-Okro-Basic | 0 | 17 | 17 | 0 | 5 |

P3-Okro-Basic has **5 non-positive CR values** (near-zero or negative Tafel readings). These are flagged but retained in the master dataset; each downstream analysis decides whether to include or exclude them (e.g., Arrhenius analysis requires CR > 0 for ln(CR)).

*Source: `data_quality_audit.csv`, columns `n_missing_Temp_C` through `n_CR_le_0`.*

### 1.3 Replicate Structure

| Sub-phase | n rows | Unique condition groups | Groups with replicates | Max replicates | Mean rows/group |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1-DoE-Blend | 28 | 7 | 5 | 9 | 4.0 |
| P1-Temperature | 30 | 30 | 0 | 1 | 1.0 |
| P1-Time | 30 | 30 | 0 | 1 | 1.0 |
| P2-Temperature | 90 | 30 | 30 | 3 | 3.0 |

| P3-Okro-Basic | 17 | 9 | 5 | 5 | 1.9 |

P2's 90 rows per sub-study are exactly **30 unique conditions × 3 replicate measurements each**. This structure confirms that grouped CV is necessary, not optional — naive random CV would have leaked replicates across train/test splits.

*Source: `replicate_structure.csv`.*

## 2. RQ1 — Scientific Convergence: Activation-Energy Analysis

> *Do independently tested green inhibitor systems exhibit consistent temperature-dependent corrosion behaviour?*

**Source:** [`arrhenius_activation_energy.csv`](Unified_Analysis/arrhenius_activation_energy.csv), [`ea_comparison.csv`](Unified_Analysis/ea_comparison.csv), [`ea_sensitivity.csv`](Unified_Analysis/ea_sensitivity.csv)

### 2.1 Arrhenius Activation Energies by Phase

| Phase | Dose groups fit | Ea mean (kJ/mol) | Ea std (kJ/mol) | Individual Ea values (kJ/mol) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P1-Temperature | 6 | 61.1 | 10.6 | 42.42, 56.14, 62.13, 66.12, 68.65, 71.20 |
| P2-Temperature | 6 | 66.5 | 16.6 | 45.36, 54.25, 60.30, 70.12, 78.37, 90.70 |
| P3-Okro-Acid | 4 | 11.2 | 9.7 | 5.46, -0.64, 15.27, 24.81 |
| P3-Okro-Basic | 3 | -180.2 | 513.4 | 76.43, 279.75, -896.75 |

*Source: `arrhenius_activation_energy.csv`.*

### 2.2 Formal Statistical Comparison (P1 vs P2 Only)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| P1 Ea mean ± SD | 61.1 ± 10.6 kJ/mol |
| P2 Ea mean ± SD | 66.5 ± 16.6 kJ/mol |
| Difference | 5.4 kJ/mol |
| Standard error of difference | 8.0 kJ/mol |
| Welch's t-statistic | -0.67 |
| Welch's p-value | **0.52** |
| Mann-Whitney U statistic | 15.0 |
| Mann-Whitney p-value | **0.70** |
| Cohen's d | -0.39 (small-to-moderate) |

**Conclusion:** The two estimates are **not statistically distinguishable** within the uncertainty of the fitted estimates (p > 0.05 by both parametric and non-parametric tests). The convergence around 61–67 kJ/mol is consistent with a surface-coverage/adsorption-dominated interpretation, but no adsorption isotherm data were collected, so no stronger mechanistic claim is made.

P3's Ea values (11.2 kJ/mol acidic; -180.2 kJ/mol basic) are **excluded from the headline convergence claim** — the per-dose-group fits are too inconsistent to trust (individual basic-media fits range from -897 to +280 kJ/mol).

*Source: `ea_comparison.csv`.*

### 2.3 Dose-Group Jackknife Sensitivity

Leave-one-dose-group-out analysis tests whether any single dose group drives the convergence:

| Phase | Excluded Ea value | Jackknife mean Ea | Remaining groups |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P1-Temperature | 42.42 | 64.85 | 5 |
| P1-Temperature | 56.14 | 62.10 | 5 |
| P1-Temperature | 62.13 | 60.91 | 5 |
| P1-Temperature | 66.12 | 60.11 | 5 |
| P1-Temperature | 68.65 | 59.60 | 5 |
| P1-Temperature | 71.20 | 59.09 | 5 |
| P2-Temperature | 45.36 | 70.75 | 5 |
| P2-Temperature | 54.25 | 68.97 | 5 |
| P2-Temperature | 60.30 | 67.76 | 5 |
| P2-Temperature | 70.12 | 65.80 | 5 |
| P2-Temperature | 78.37 | 64.15 | 5 |
| P2-Temperature | 90.70 | 61.68 | 5 |

**P1 jackknife range:** 59.1–64.8 kJ/mol. **P2 jackknife range:** 61.7–70.7 kJ/mol. No single dose group drives the convergence — the Ea estimates remain in the 59–71 kJ/mol band regardless of which group is excluded.

*Source: `ea_sensitivity.csv`.*

## 3. RQ2 — Environmental Drivers: Predictor Dominance

> *How does the dominant predictor of corrosion rate change with temperature, exposure time, inhibitor concentration, and solution chemistry?*

**Source:** [`correlation_comparison.csv`](Unified_Analysis/correlation_comparison.csv), [`predictor_ablation.csv`](Unified_Analysis/predictor_ablation.csv), [`interaction_effects.csv`](Unified_Analysis/interaction_effects.csv)

### 3.1 Correlation of CR with Environmental Variables

| Study | n | r(CR, Temp) | r(CR, Time) | r(CR, Dose) | Dose unit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P1-Temperature | 30 | **0.907** | — | -0.241 | ppm |
| P2-Temperature | 90 | **0.770** | — | -0.170 | ppm |
| P3-Okro-Acid | 17 | 0.336 | — | -0.350 | ppm |
| P3-Okro-Basic | 17 | -0.377 | — | 0.050 | ppm |
| P1-Time | 30 | — | -0.014 | **-0.696** | ppm |
| P2-Time | 90 | — | -0.223 | **-0.587** | ppm |
| P1-DoE-Blend | 28 | — | 0.598 | — | mL_blend |

Temperature dominates in both gravimetric temperature-varying phases. Dose/concentration dominates in both time-varying phases. P3 correlations are weak and directionally inconsistent.

*Source: `correlation_comparison.csv`.*

### 3.2 Three-Layer Predictor-Dominance Evidence

| Phase | Layer 1: Correlation | Layer 2: Permutation importance | Layer 3: Ablation R² drop | Agreement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1-Temperature | Temp_C (r=0.907) | Temp_C (1.879) | Temp_C (3.740) | **AGREE — temperature dominant** |
| P2-Temperature | Temp_C (r=0.770) | Temp_C (1.796) | Temp_C (3.785) | **AGREE — temperature dominant** |
| P3-Okro-Acid | Dose_Value (r=-0.350) | Temp_C (0.595) | Dose_Value (0.609) | MIXED — no dominant factor claimed |
| P3-Okro-Basic | Temp_C (r=-0.377) | Temp_C (0.874) | Molarity_M (4260.4) | MIXED — no dominant factor claimed |
| P1-Time | Dose_Value (r=-0.696) | Dose_Value (2.100) | Dose_Value (40.110) | **AGREE — dose dominant** |
| P2-Time | Dose_Value (r=-0.587) | Dose_Value (1.053) | Dose_Value (0.335) | **AGREE — dose dominant** |

Temperature dominance is claimed **only** for P1-Temperature and P2-Temperature, where all three independent evidence layers agree. P3 produces mixed evidence — no universal dominant factor is asserted.

*Source: `predictor_ablation.csv`, columns `permutation_importance` and `R2_drop_when_removed`.*

### 3.3 Interaction Effects

| Phase | n | Dose×Temp interaction coefficient | p-value | Significant? | Model R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| P1-Temperature | 30 | -0.0022 | 0.624 | No | 0.882 |
| P2-Temperature | 90 | -0.0021 | 0.553 | No | 0.624 |

No significant interaction between dose and temperature in either gravimetric temperature phase — concentration does not measurably modify the temperature effect in these phases.

*Source: `interaction_effects.csv`.*

## 4. RQ3 — Cross-Phase Generalization

> *Can a model trained across some experimental phases generalize to a phase it has not seen?*

**Source:** [`model_leaderboard.csv`](Unified_Analysis/model_leaderboard.csv), [`leave_one_phase_out_results.csv`](Unified_Analysis/leave_one_phase_out_results.csv), [`p1p2_vs_p1p2p3.csv`](Unified_Analysis/p1p2_vs_p1p2p3.csv), [`phase_identity_ablation.csv`](Unified_Analysis/phase_identity_ablation.csv), [`phase_identity_permutation_share.csv`](Unified_Analysis/phase_identity_permutation_share.csv)

### 4.1 Validation Leakage: Standard CV vs Grouped CV

| Config | Model | Standard CV R² | Grouped CV R² | Standard CV MAE | Grouped CV MAE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A_P1 | XGBoost | 0.983 | 0.372 | 3.9 | 17.8 |
| A_P1 | CatBoost | 0.965 | 0.571 | 5.4 | 15.7 |
| B_P2 | RandomForest | 0.965 | -0.236 | 11.3 | 45.3 |
| B_P2 | CatBoost | 0.958 | 0.269 | 13.5 | 38.3 |
| D_P1P2 | CatBoost | 0.971 | 0.421 | 7.2 | 29.3 |
| E_P1P2P3 | CatBoost | 0.608 | 0.041 | 14.9 | 32.8 |

Standard random CV substantially overestimates performance. The gap is most dramatic for P2 (RandomForest: 0.965 → -0.236), confirming that replicate leakage inflates apparent model quality. Grouped CV is the more defensible basis for any generalization claim.

*Source: `model_leaderboard.csv`, selected representative rows.*

### 4.2 Leave-One-Phase-Out Generalization

| Training phases | Held-out phase | Best model | R² | MAE | RMSE |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P1+P2 | P3 | CatBoost | **-0.24** | 83.7 | 164.1 |
| P1+P3 | P2 | XGBoost | **0.40** | 40.0 | 77.2 |
| P2+P3 | P1 | Ridge | **0.57** | 34.2 | 42.5 |

Transfer is **direction-dependent**:

- **P1+P2 → P3** fails (negative R² across all 4 models). This direction requires simultaneous extrapolation in molarity and an entirely unseen medium (Basic/NaOH), combined with a different measurement technique, inhibitor system, and experimental structure.
- **P2+P3 → P1** performs best (R² = 0.57), requiring only temperature and time extrapolation, not medium or dose extrapolation.
- Every direction involves an unseen inhibitor system — cross-phase generalization is **not** equivalent to controlled unseen-inhibitor-chemistry testing (the two are confounded).

*Source: `leave_one_phase_out_results.csv`, best-R² row per train/test direction.*

### 4.3 Effect of Adding P3 to the Pooled Model

| Model | CV scheme | P1+P2 R² | P1+P2+P3 R² | R² change | P1+P2 MAE | P1+P2+P3 MAE | MAE change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ridge | Standard | 0.719 | 0.498 | -0.222 | 28.3 | 35.8 | +7.5 |
| RandomForest | Standard | 0.941 | 0.620 | -0.321 | 11.6 | 17.0 | +5.4 |
| XGBoost | Standard | 0.964 | 0.364 | -0.600 | 8.2 | 15.5 | +7.3 |
| CatBoost | Standard | 0.971 | 0.608 | -0.363 | 7.2 | 14.9 | +7.7 |
| Ridge | Grouped | -0.319 | -0.985 | -0.667 | 35.1 | 42.2 | +7.1 |
| RandomForest | Grouped | -0.169 | 0.057 | +0.226 | 35.1 | 36.5 | +1.4 |
| XGBoost | Grouped | 0.404 | 0.052 | -0.352 | 28.5 | 35.2 | +6.8 |
| CatBoost | Grouped | 0.421 | 0.041 | -0.380 | 29.3 | 32.8 | +3.5 |

Adding P3 **hurts** pooled performance in **6 of 8** model×CV-scheme comparisons. This is consistent with P3 representing a genuine experimental and measurement-regime shift, not a pipeline failure.

*Source: `p1p2_vs_p1p2p3.csv`.*

### 4.4 Phase-Identity Ablation

Removing identity features (`Technique`, `Medium_Type`, `Inhibitor_System`) tests whether models learn from real environmental variables or phase shortcuts:

**P1+P2 (D vs F — same-technique phases):** Identity removal changes R² by < 0.03 in every model×CV combination. Identity features carry only **1.2%** of total permutation importance — the model is learning from real environmental variables, not phase identity.

**P1+P2+P3 (E vs G — mixed-technique phases):** Identity removal causes larger swings (up to 0.26 R² drop for CatBoost standard CV). Identity features carry **6.0%** of permutation importance — most plausibly because they help the model recognize the Tafel measurement scale difference, not because of a shortcut.

| Full config | Reduced config | Model | CV scheme | Full R² | Reduced R² | R² drop |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| D_P1P2 | F_P1P2_noIdentity | Ridge | Standard | 0.719 | 0.718 | 0.001 |
| D_P1P2 | F_P1P2_noIdentity | CatBoost | Standard | 0.971 | 0.971 | 0.000 |
| D_P1P2 | F_P1P2_noIdentity | CatBoost | Grouped | 0.421 | 0.448 | -0.027 |
| E_P1P2P3 | G_P1P2P3_noIdentity | CatBoost | Standard | 0.608 | 0.353 | 0.255 |
| E_P1P2P3 | G_P1P2P3_noIdentity | XGBoost | Grouped | 0.052 | -0.330 | 0.382 |

*Source: `phase_identity_ablation.csv` and `phase_identity_permutation_share.csv`.*

## 5. RQ4 — Measurement Robustness

> *How does changing from gravimetric weight loss to Tafel electrochemical measurement affect predictive reliability?*

**Source:** [`error_stratification.csv`](Unified_Analysis/error_stratification.csv), [`model_leaderboard.csv`](Unified_Analysis/model_leaderboard.csv)

### 5.1 Error Stratification by Phase, Technique, Medium, and Temperature

| Stratification | Value | n | MAE | MAE std | CR mean |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Phase_Group | P1 | 88 | 15.4 | 31.8 | 36.3 |
| Phase_Group | P2 | 180 | 30.3 | 58.9 | 63.6 |
| Phase_Group | P3 | 34 | 91.2 | 172.8 | 77.8 |
| Technique | Weight loss | 268 | 25.4 | 52.0 | 54.7 |
| Technique | Tafel (electrochemical) | 34 | 91.2 | 172.8 | 77.8 |
| Medium_Type | Acid | 285 | 27.7 | 61.4 | 56.4 |
| Medium_Type | Basic | 17 | 119.0 | 199.3 | 71.5 |
| temp_bin | ≤40°C | 50 | 45.3 | 146.6 | 45.2 |
| temp_bin | 40–60°C | 74 | 37.0 | 39.9 | 77.1 |
| temp_bin | >60°C | 30 | 131.3 | 93.1 | 255.2 |
| dose_bin | ≤100 | 126 | 22.2 | 41.2 | 57.3 |
| dose_bin | 100–250 | 116 | 46.9 | 109.1 | 62.7 |
| dose_bin | >250 | 60 | 27.9 | 60.9 | 46.6 |

Error concentrates heavily in **P3/Tafel/Basic-medium/high-temperature** segments. The Tafel-technique MAE (91.2) is **3.6× higher** than weight-loss MAE (25.4). Basic-medium MAE (119.0) is **4.3× higher** than acid-medium MAE (27.7). Above 60°C, MAE reaches 131.3 — the model's worst-performing region.

Global performance numbers hide these systematic regional weaknesses.

*Source: `error_stratification.csv`.*

### 5.2 P3-Alone Model Performance

P3 alone produces **negative R²** for every model under both CV schemes:

| Model | Standard CV R² | Grouped CV R² |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ridge | -3.44 | -5.06 |
| RandomForest | -1.76 | -8.87 |
| XGBoost | -3.37 | -7.86 |
| CatBoost | -1.61 | -5.10 |

This is an honest limitation, interpreted jointly with n=17/medium and the multiple simultaneous experimental/measurement-regime differences — **not** as proof that Okro extract is a weaker inhibitor.

*Source: `model_leaderboard.csv`, Config C_P3.*

## 6. Validation Integrity

**Source:** [`permutation_null_test.csv`](Unified_Analysis/permutation_null_test.csv), [`repeated_cv_stability.csv`](Unified_Analysis/repeated_cv_stability.csv), [`model_simplicity_test.csv`](Unified_Analysis/model_simplicity_test.csv), [`target_leakage_audit.csv`](Unified_Analysis/target_leakage_audit.csv)

### 6.1 Permutation Null Test

| Config | Model | n perms | Real R² (grouped) | Null R² mean | Null R² 95th pct | Empirical p |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| D_P1P2 | RandomForest | 20 | -0.174 | -0.583 | -0.385 | 0.048 |
| E_P1P2P3 | RandomForest | 20 | 0.019 | -0.488 | -0.230 | 0.048 |

The pooled models' grouped-CV performance exceeds the 95th percentile of a shuffled-target null distribution (empirical p ≈ 0.048 in both cases). **The signal is real**, even where the raw R² looks modest.

*Source: `permutation_null_test.csv`.*

### 6.2 Repeated CV Stability

| Config | Model | n repeats | Mean R² | Std R² | Min R² | Max R² |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| D_P1P2 | RandomForest | 5 | -0.174 | 0.005 | -0.180 | -0.165 |
| E_P1P2P3 | RandomForest | 5 | 0.019 | 0.025 | -0.002 | 0.056 |

The grouped-CV results are **stable across 5 reshuffled fold assignments** — not an artifact of one lucky split. The P1+P2 configuration has very low variance (std = 0.005); the P1+P2+P3 configuration has somewhat higher variance (std = 0.025) but remains consistent.

*Source: `repeated_cv_stability.csv`.*

### 6.3 Model Complexity Justification

| Config | CV scheme | Ridge R² | Best complex model | Best complex R² | R² gain over Ridge | Meaningful (>0.05)? |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| A_P1 | Grouped | -1.664 | CatBoost | 0.571 | 2.236 | Yes |
| A_P1 | Standard | 0.911 | XGBoost | 0.983 | 0.072 | Yes |
| B_P2 | Grouped | -3.801 | CatBoost | 0.269 | 4.070 | Yes |
| B_P2 | Standard | 0.698 | XGBoost | 0.969 | 0.271 | Yes |
| C_P3 | Grouped | -5.061 | CatBoost | -5.104 | -0.043 | **No** |
| C_P3 | Standard | -3.443 | CatBoost | -1.614 | 1.828 | Yes |
| D_P1P2 | Grouped | -0.319 | CatBoost | 0.421 | 0.739 | Yes |
| E_P1P2P3 | Grouped | -0.985 | RandomForest | 0.057 | 1.042 | Yes |

Model complexity is generally justified (>0.05 R² gain over Ridge in **13 of 14** configurations), **except for P3 alone under grouped CV**, where no model works regardless of complexity.

*Source: `model_simplicity_test.csv`.*

### 6.4 Target Leakage Confirmation

`IE_percent` is mathematically derived from `CR_mm_yr` (blank-comparison formula). Verification on 150 P2 comparisons confirms agreement to within **0.28 percentage points** (max absolute difference: 0.28 pp). This confirms `IE_percent` must never be used as a predictor of CR, which the modelling pipeline already respects.

*Source: `target_leakage_audit.csv` (150 P2-Temperature/P2-Time rows, column `abs_diff`).*

## 7. Standalone Finding: P1 DoE Blend Optimization

**Source:** [`dosage_efficiency_index.csv`](Unified_Analysis/dosage_efficiency_index.csv)

### 7.1 DoE Optimal Point

P1's DoE optimal blend point achieves:

- **CR ≈ 1.64 mm/yr**
- **IE ≈ 87.6%**

in its native mL-blend dosage units. This is reported as a standalone finding — it is **not** benchmarked against P2's or P3's ppm-dosed results because no validated mL-to-ppm conversion exists.

### 7.2 Dosage Efficiency Index (ppm-based studies only)

| Study | n | Mean IE% | Mean ppm tested | IE%/ppm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1-Time | 25 | 81.2 | 150.0 | 0.729 |
| P1-Temperature | 25 | 43.8 | 150.0 | 0.339 |
| P2-Time | 75 | 60.6 | 250.0 | 0.323 |
| P2-Temperature | 75 | 44.1 | 250.0 | 0.241 |

Dosage efficiency is consistently higher in time-based phases than temperature-based phases for the same inhibitor family. A given ppm of inhibitor buys more IE at moderate temperature than at elevated temperature — a quantified way to state that heat degrades inhibitor economics.

P1-DoE-Blend (mean IE 81.7% at 15.0 mL mean dose) is excluded from this ranking because its dose unit (mL of blend) is not comparable to ppm.

*Source: `dosage_efficiency_index.csv`.*

## 8. Interpolation and Extrapolation Analysis

**Source:** [`interpolation_extrapolation.csv`](Unified_Analysis/interpolation_extrapolation.csv)

Understanding **where** the leave-one-phase-out models interpolate vs. extrapolate explains the transfer pattern:

### P1+P2 → P3 (worst transfer, R² = -0.24)

| Variable | Train range | Test range | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dose_Value | 0–450 | 50–200 | Interpolation |
| Temp_C | 30–80 | 30–60 | Interpolation |
| Molarity_M | 0.5–1.5 | 1.0–2.5 | **Extrapolation** |
| Medium_Type | Acid only | Acid + **Basic** | **Extrapolation (unseen)** |

### P1+P3 → P2 (moderate transfer, R² = 0.40)

| Variable | Train range | Test range | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dose_Value | 0–250 | 0–450 | **Extrapolation** |
| Temp_C | 30–80 | 30–70 | Interpolation |
| Time_h | 5–125 | 3–15 | **Extrapolation** |
| Molarity_M | 1.0–2.5 | 0.5–1.5 | **Extrapolation** |
| Medium_Type | Acid + Basic | Acid only | Interpolation |

### P2+P3 → P1 (best transfer, R² = 0.57)

| Variable | Train range | Test range | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dose_Value | 0–450 | 0–250 | Interpolation |
| Temp_C | 30–70 | 40–80 | **Extrapolation** |
| Time_h | 3–15 | 5–125 | **Extrapolation** |
| Molarity_M | 0.5–2.5 | 1.0–1.0 | Interpolation |
| Medium_Type | Acid + Basic | Acid only | Interpolation |

The worst-performing direction (P1+P2 → P3) is the only one requiring extrapolation into an **entirely unseen medium** (Basic/NaOH). The best-performing direction (P2+P3 → P1) only requires extrapolating in temperature and time, not in medium or dose — explaining the asymmetry.

*Source: `interpolation_extrapolation.csv`.*

## 9. Evidence Tiers

### Core Evidence (P1 + P2)

| Claim | Status | Key evidence |
|---|---|---|
